topic: Career angle: AI isn't firing people yet. It's quietly not hiring them.
post:
AI isn't firing people yet.
It's quietly not hiring them. 🚪

This week, the Bank of England published new findings on AI and jobs in the UK.

What it found, per The Register and Resultsense:
1️⃣ Firms surveyed reported almost no overall effect from AI on employment so far.
2️⃣ But the Bank's regional contacts say AI is making firms less likely to hire, or to replace staff who leave.
3️⃣ And not much more likely to fire anyone, so far.

That's a quiet shift. No big layoff headline. Just fewer open doors. 🔍

My career take 👇
If hiring slows, the people who move up are the ones already inside, using AI to do more.

Why it matters:
When roles aren't backfilled, the work doesn't disappear. It lands on the team. The person who can absorb it with AI becomes hard to replace. 💪

Practical takeaway:
This week, pick one task a former colleague used to do. Write down how you'd handle it with AI, and show your manager. 📝

Is your team replacing people who leave? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
